question: What does the most recent news article on proteinatlas.org report: which journal was the study published in, who led the team, and what did they identify?

The latest article (September 10, 2026) is an "Image of the Week" post about PDX1 in the pancreas, and it's not reporting on a published research study. To check whether the most recent article in the "Publication" category is what the question is referring to, I'll go check the Publication article from August 27, 2026.

I checked the Human Protein Atlas news archive. The most recent news article listed is dated 2026-09-10: "Multiplex tissue image of the month – PDX1 in pancreas" (https://www.proteinatlas.org/news/2026-09-10/multiplex-tissue-image-of-the-month-pdx1-in-pancreas).

**What it reports:** It is an "Image of the Week" post, not a report of a research publication. It describes showing the expression of the beta-cell transcription factor PDX1 in the endocrine pancreas using multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC/IF) with HPA's pancreas panel — PDX1 (green) localizing to the nucleus of beta cells (magenta), with alpha cells (cyan) also visualized. It invites readers to the mIHC/IF method page for details.

**Regarding your specific sub-questions, the pages I opened do not answer them for this article:**
- **Journal:** The article mentions no journal — it is an image showcase, not a publication announcement.
- **Who led the team:** No team or team leader is named anywhere in the article.
- **What they identified:** Nothing of the form "identified X" is reported; it simply displays PDX1 localization (nuclear in beta-cells) in pancreas tissue.

For context, the most recent article that *does* announce a publication (https://www.proteinatlas.org/news/2026-08-27/the-multiplex-tissue-resource-provides-deeper-spatial-insight-into-protein-expression, dated 2026-08-27) reports a new article in **Protein Science** describing the HPA Multiplex tissue resource — but even that post does not name who led the team, so I can't answer that part from the pages available.
